messages.subject: Continuous Covariate
parts:
Hello,

I am including a covariate in my analysis that is continuous. Therefore, it should be a non-factor in the MCDS Engine. However, the resulting detection models shows three curves as if the continuous variable was binned (see image). I'm just reaching out to get any advice on what might be happening. I've run the similar analyses in R, and the resulting graph shows each observation as a point with the corresponding distance and detection probability. I'd like to produce a similar graphic. Maybe there's a formula in the output that I can use in R to graph the probability of detection for each observation based the distance and covariate value?

Thank you,
Kammie

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Continuous Covariate
parts:
Kammie

When using a continuous covariate in the detection function using Distance for Windows software, here is the description of the plot taken from Chapter 9 of the Users Guide:

Plot: Example Detection Functions. If there are any non-factor covariates, then the above plots show the detection function (or pdf) averaged over the observed covariate levels. Depending on the observed covariates, the shape of these functions can be quite different from the detection function given fixed covariate values. So, for each non-factor covariate, the MCDS engine outputs a plot showing 3 example detection functions. These are evaluated at the 25th, 50th and 75th quartiles of the covariate. If there is more than one non-factor covariate, the values of the other covariates are fixed at the 50th percentile.

If you wish to duplicate the plot in R, there is a function add_df_covar_line()​. An example of its use can be found in one of our online vignettes:


http://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-spec-covar/species-covariate-distill.html

Hope that helps.
